strategy_1.name: greater deployment funding
strategy_1.property_1: 80% of the additional climate budget funds emissions-reduction deployment
strategy_1.property_2: 20% of the additional climate budget funds carbon-removal research
strategy_1.candidate: I support allocating 80% to emissions-reduction deployment and 20% to carbon-removal research.
arguments: Prioritizing deployment can reduce emissions sooner, limiting their accumulation in the atmosphere.
Greater deployment funding reduces dependence on uncertain future carbon-removal capabilities.
Deploying available measures can deliver benefits while carbon-removal research continues at a smaller scale.
Reducing emissions now can lower the amount of carbon that must be removed later.
Deployment funding can help overcome practical barriers to implementing existing emissions-reduction measures.
This allocation prioritizes nearer-term action while preserving some investment in future removal options.

strategy_2.name: greater research funding
strategy_2.property_1: 50% of the additional climate budget funds emissions-reduction deployment
strategy_2.property_2: 50% of the additional climate budget funds carbon-removal research
strategy_2.candidate: I support allocating 50% to emissions-reduction deployment and 50% to carbon-removal research.
arguments: Greater research funding can help develop ways to address emissions that remain difficult to eliminate.
Investing earlier in research allows more time to investigate the limitations of carbon-removal methods.
Research can clarify which removal approaches are feasible before larger deployment commitments are made.
Developing removal capabilities can expand future options if emissions reductions fall short.
Research funding may improve removal efficiency and reduce future costs, although success is uncertain.
This allocation maintains substantial deployment funding while investing more in future removal options.

title: Immediate emissions reduction versus future carbon removal
